verdict.rationale: Snyk documents its own organization-level custom role templates for service accounts. One permits only basic CLI commands such as `snyk test`/`snyk monitor`, and a read-only variant blocks `snyk monitor`, which gives scoped, least-privilege non-human credentials. Role-based access control also appears in its plans. The evidence frames these for CI/CD pipelines rather than AI agents, and does not document the token issuance flow itself. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of issuing API tokens for service accounts, agent-specific credential scoping (e.g., for the MCP server or Studio), expiry/rotation controls, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: This Organization-level role allows service accounts in CI/CD pipelines to run basic Snyk CLI commands.
This Organization-level role blocks the use of `snyk monitor`.
The role grants permissions to run `snyk test` to check Projects for vulnerabilities and `snyk monitor`
